subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu message send silently drops unsupported attachment params (file/filePath/attachments/…) and returns ok:true — attachment never sent

question: Should Feishu preserve a strict `media`-only contract with explicit errors for file-like aliases, or should OpenClaw standardize a shared alias contract across channels first?
rationale: Both paths prevent false-success attachment sends, but the durable cross-channel tool contract determines whether aliases are compatibility behavior or unsupported input.

options.title: Fail fast on unsupported attachment intent
options.body: Keep `media` as the Feishu contract and return a descriptive error whenever file-like attachment parameters or malformed media are supplied.

options.title: Standardize aliases centrally
options.body: Define and document one shared attachment alias contract, then route Feishu and sibling channels through that canonical parser.

recommendation.title: Fail fast on unsupported attachment intent
recommendation.body: Keep `media` as the Feishu contract and return a descriptive error whenever file-like attachment parameters or malformed media are supplied.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter has the strongest concrete evidence for the intended user-facing recovery behavior, while code ownership needs direct current-main history inspection.
